directive.quote: The place side. No place route serves /a/<address>/installations/<id>/… from the installation's Namespace files yet, and no place posts its origins row yet.

preserve: a page read is answered only for a live installation, from its own files: a path in its one checked form, a folder's index, a folder without its slash sent on with 308, a single-page site's extensionless page answered by its index outside actions/capabilities/api
every answer carries its media type, nosniff, the referrer policy and no-store, and a page its content security policy
a renamed name sends a page read on (301) to the name it moved to, with its path and query; other requests stay the installation's
a domain is believed only by the _trillion-verify TXT record the resolver reads, its strings taken whole
a reserved, view-shaped (--) or code-shaped name is held by nobody; the first holder of a name keeps it
allowed_deltas: the installation's files are the account's own files under /installations/<id>/, and whether it is live is whether the account's signed origins list names it, instead of central KV routes and an R2 bucket
the TXT value names the account's address (trillion-account=<address>) instead of a stored random token, and is read over plain DNS from the system's resolvers instead of one vendor's DNS-over-HTTPS
a name is held while its account is live and for name_hold_ms after, in the forwarder's memory, instead of forever in a central list: the forwarder stores nothing (docs/PRINCIPLES.md rule 3)
a whole answer is bounded by one session message (most_answer_bytes); a larger file is read by byte range
the visitor count, shop, placed capabilities, linked routes, views and site backend are not served by the engine: they are Workshop tools
banned_substitutions: a central name or domain list kept by the forwarder
a vendor's DNS or certificate API in the engine
a second copy of the Workshop's name or domain checks in the engine beyond the refusal the forwarder must make
